record.paper_title: On an Open Question in Recovering Sturm--Liouville-Type Operators with Delay
record.original_question: Determine the uniqueness or nonuniqueness behavior of the delayed Sturm-Liouville two-spectra inverse problem for arbitrarily small positive delays a, where -y''(x)+q(x)y(x-a)=lambda y(x) is close to the classical a=0 Sturm-Liouville equation -y''(x)+q(x)y(x)=lambda y(x). For small a>0, does the pair of spectra {lambda_{n,0}} and {lambda_{n,1}} recover q uniquely, and if not, what iso-bispectral families occur?

evidence.quote: One of the first results in the inverse spectral theory says that the spectra of two boundary value problems for one and the same Sturm--Liouville equation with one common boundary condition: $-y''(x)+q(x)y(x)=\lambda y(x), \quad y(0)=y^{(j)}(\pi)=0, \quad j=0,1,$ uniquely determine the potential $q(x).$
It is especially important to investigate the case of arbitrarily small values of $a$ making the problem ''close'' to the classical case~(\ref{0}).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the functional-differential equation
  -y''(x) + q(x) y(x-a) = λ y(x),  x ∈ (0,π),
where a ∈ (0,π) is a constant delay, q ∈ L_2(0,π) is a real-valued potential with q(x) = 0 for x ∈ (0,a), and y(x-a) is interpreted as 0 on (0,a). For j ∈ {0,1}, let {λ_{n,j}}_{n≥1} denote the spectrum of the boundary value problem consisting of this equation together with the boundary conditions
  y(0) = 0,    y^(j)(π) = 0.

The classical (a = 0) result of Borg states that the two spectra {λ_{n,0}} and {λ_{n,1}} uniquely determine q.

Question: Investigate the regime of arbitrarily small positive delays a > 0. Does the pair of spectra ({λ_{n,0}}, {λ_{n,1}}) uniquely determine q for all sufficiently small a > 0? If not, exhibit and characterize the iso-bispectral families, i.e., distinct potentials q ≠ q̃ (with the same vanishing on (0,a)) that produce identical pairs of spectra for the corresponding two boundary value problems.
artifact.status_search_result: The question was answered negatively: for arbitrarily small delays, the two-spectra inverse problem for the delayed Sturm–Liouville operator does not uniquely recover the potential. Djurić and Buterin (2021, "Iso-bispectral potentials for Sturm–Liouville-type operators with small delay", Nonlinear Anal. RWA, also arXiv:2102.08149) constructed infinite families of iso-bispectral potentials, showing non-uniqueness persists as a → 0. Related counterexamples were given for the Neumann case (arXiv:2101.08557).

status_evidence.title: Iso-bispectral potentials for Sturm–Liouville-type operators with small delay
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs infinite families of iso-bispectral potentials, demonstrating non-uniqueness for arbitrarily small delays.
status_evidence.claim: Non-uniqueness holds for the two-spectra inverse problem with arbitrarily small delay; iso-bispectral families exist.

status_evidence.title: On non-uniqueness of recovering Sturm-Liouville operators with delay and the Neumann boundary condition at zero
status_evidence.snippet: Counterexample to uniqueness in the delayed Sturm-Liouville inverse problem with Neumann boundary condition.
status_evidence.claim: Related non-uniqueness result for the Neumann boundary condition case.
